title: RL-Phase Contamination Signal: Does Output-Entropy Collapse Appear on Safety Tasks?

original_idea.body:
# RL-Phase Contamination Signal: Does Output-Entropy Collapse Appear on Safety Tasks?

**Problem:** A recent paper detects RL-post-training contamination via entropy collapse into sparse output modes (RL-MIA / Self-Critique), demonstrated on math/logic. Whether the same entropy-collapse signature flags contamination on safety-relevant tasks (refusals, jailbreak responses) is untested.

**Direction:** For an open RL-tuned model vs its base/SFT version, measure token-level output entropy on a held-out safety task set vs a likely-seen safety set. Test whether the entropy-collapse contamination signal from the paper distinguishes them, using a simple per-prompt entropy statistic and threshold.

**Why it matters:** RLHF-tuned models dominate deployment and their safety scores may be contaminated through post-training, an under-explored vector. A cheap entropy-based detector applicable to open RL models lets external auditors flag inflated safety claims without retraining.

**Relevant context:** Detecting Data Contamination from Reinforcement Learning Post-training for Large Language Models (arXiv:2510.09259) introduces Self-Critique and RL-MIA based on post-RL output-entropy collapse.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (entropy-collapse detector for safety contamination) but the safety-task transfer link is speculative and indirect.

novelty.reasoning: Transfers a recent detector to safety tasks; partly open.
